_schema.purpose: Single canonical register of everything this project has measured, refuted, or left untried. Machine-readable source of truth; FINDINGS.md is GENERATED from it by findings.py and must never be hand-edited.

fields.kind: law | lever | dead_end | contradiction | untried | external
fields.claim: one sentence, falsifiable, stated as what is true
fields.magnitude: the number that matters, with units
fields.evidence: prereg number, file:line, or external source
fields.scope: the hardware and model class the claim was measured on - a claim outside its scope is a guess
fields.status: established | shipped | refuted | open | staked | untested
fields.wired_into: where it reaches shipped code, or null

untried_extra_fields.predicted_effect: staked magnitude - written BEFORE the test, so a miss is visible
untried_extra_fields.why_it_is_promising: which established finding implies this lever should work

_schema.reference_box: i5-7600K, GTX 1060 6GB, 16GB DDR4-3000, SATA MX500, PCIe 3.0 x16 @ 12.2 GB/s

laws.claim: Decode speed is bandwidth-bound: tok/s = eta(tier) x BW / active-bytes-per-token.
laws.scope: VRAM/RAM/disk tiers, dense and MoE, one GPU

laws.claim: KV cache is a first-class bandwidth consumer priced at its own efficiency, ETA_KV = 0.70.
laws.magnitude: tg32 20.35 -> 6.30 tok/s from d0 to d16384

laws.claim: Quantization fragility is measurable but NOT predictable from architecture; attention and SSM tensors are fragile, embeddings and FFN are not.
laws.magnitude: depth-aware recipe protects attn_.*/ssm_.* (+shexp/nextn on MoE)

laws.claim: Effective rank, not bit-count, is the state variable of quantization; incoherence is rank-conditional.
laws.magnitude: gauge hypothesis refuted; cache phase-transition observed

laws.claim: Prefill is compute-bound, so the bit ladder runs BACKWARDS there - fewer bits is SLOWER.
laws.wired_into: documented; planner does not yet model prefill bits

laws.claim: The VRAM claimants - weights, KV cache, compute buffer - are FUNGIBLE, and fungibility is placement-specific: only a configuration that is actually starved can spend the refund.
laws.magnitude: evicting KV recovers 2.42x prefill on the split, and nothing (-3%) on all-experts-to-CPU

laws.claim: REFUTED (2026-07-27). Was: 'there is no single best placement - there is a Pareto frontier selected by the prompt:generation ratio.' Re-measured with every cell in ONE session, ONE configuration wins at every ratio.
laws.magnitude: The claimed spread shrank three times, each time from correcting one of our own measurement errors: 2.25x (contained a cell measured past the compute-buffer cliff) -> 1.33x (corrected to ub 512) -> 1.23x (all cells in one session) -> gone (the surviving alternative wins by 0.44 tok/s against combined error bars of 0.456, i.e. 0.96 sigma). Same-session table: split+ub1024+KV-in-VRAM 386.04/21.58 dominates all-experts-CPU 381.82/19.79 and evict-KV 381.60/17.95.
laws.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py:MOE_FRONTIER (one row) · tests/smoke.py:t_workload_frontier_is_pareto (rewritten to assert the collapse)
laws.why_it_was_wrong: The frontier was an ARTEFACT of never measuring split + KV-in-VRAM at ub 1024. That cell had been benchmarked only at ub 2048 (past the cliff, 161.59 pp) and ub 512 (307.13 pp), and was recorded as 'dominated' - a claim that silently inherited the scope of the sweep that produced it. It really meant 'dominated AT ub 2048'. Excluding a configuration is also a claim, and it needs a scope like any other.

laws.claim: llama.cpp's CUDA compute buffer is exactly linear in the ubatch, so demand grows smoothly while VRAM supply ends abruptly - producing a cliff, not a taper.
laws.magnitude: 0.5874 MiB per ubatch token, to four figures; -45% prefill in one -ub step

laws.claim: ggml offers host-resident weights to CUDA once the ubatch clears 32 tokens, so host weights cross PCIe once per UBATCH rather than once per token.
laws.magnitude: +73% prefill at ub 512 -> 2048 with experts on CPU

laws.claim: The Gemma MLP weight element stream is white - there is no intra-tensor redundancy for VQ to exploit.

THE DECODE WALL, measured basis: every active byte on a tier transits its bus once per token, so tok/s <= 1/sum(bytes_i/BW_i). On MEASURED bandwidth (26.1 GB/s pure-read stream, not the 48 spec) the flagship's raw-decode wall is 41.1 tok/s; we measure 22.25 (54%). The wall is EXCEEDABLE only by breaking the axiom: speculation verified 50.04 tok/s - 22% above it - in the copy regime.
laws.magnitude: Decomposition (prereg #27): stream measured 26.1 GB/s pure read / 30.4 copy, one thread already saturating; pure-CPU decode 14.06 tok/s = 17.1 GB/s effective = 66% of stream (kernel+MLP share); GPU<->CPU sync excess 7.4-11.1 ms/token = 17-25% of the token. The spec-sheet walls (69.5 / 52.9) were fiction: DDR4-3000 promises 48 GB/s this controller cannot deliver.
laws.evidence: prereg #27 (decomposition + measured stream), prereg #28 (the exceedance), prereg #25 (the 22.25)
laws.scope: reference box, flagship model. The axiom underneath is tier-agnostic: every active byte on a tier must transit that tier's bus once per token, so tok/s <= 1 / sum(bytes_i / BW_i). No runtime can beat that without reducing bytes or amortising them across tokens.
laws.wired_into: the research agenda: U-09 is the decomposition
laws.what_this_rules_in_and_out: RULED OUT: any raw-decode runtime gain past 1.85x on this box (41.1 ceiling), and in practice far less - the CPU path already runs at 66% of real stream, and sync is worth at most ~29%. D-05's no-fork verdict survives with that measured asterisk. RULED IN and MEASURED: exceeding the wall via speculation (50.04, prereg #28) and skipping prefill via prefix caching (29x TTFT, prereg #29). The remaining breakthroughs are not in moving bytes better - they are in not moving bytes at all.
laws.gap_attribution_final: The 22.25->41.1 gap is now FULLY attributed (prereg #31): ~40% is the MoE EXPERT-PATH CODE in ggml's CPU MUL_MAT_ID (prereg #32 REFUTED the prefetch story: shuffled 2MB slab reads lose nothing, and the MoE path saturates at 16 GB/s where dense reaches 28.4 identically threaded); 17-25% is GPU<->CPU sync (needs async transfer code, scheduling measured dead); 0% scheduling; 0% K-format choice (Q2_K and Q4_K_M tie at the wall on CPU). On stock llama.cpp this box's raw decode is FINISHED - every remaining percent costs upstream engineering bounded at 1.85x combined, while speculation already delivers 2.3-2.5x by not reading bytes at all.
laws.exceedance_record: The wall (41.1 tok/s raw decode on measured bandwidth) is now exceeded by 2.2x: 90.33 tok/s with ngram speculation at size-m 384 (prereg #36), byte-identical output. The remaining ceiling is the batched verify forward, measured at ~405-445 tok/s (#26) - so speculation itself still runs at ~1/4.5 of ITS ceiling, and the binding constraint there is draft availability from the n-gram store, not hardware.

laws.claim: THE PREFILL WALL. Batched prefill converges to ~405-445 t/s on this GPU regardless of placement - 65-67% of the card's theoretical FLOP ceiling, which is as close as real kernels get on Pascal. Prefill on this box is CLOSED except for levers that cut FLOPs themselves.
laws.magnitude: GTX 1060 6GB ~4.4 TFLOPS FP32; MoE k=8 active 3.3B -> ~6.6 GFLOP/token -> 667 t/s at 100%. Measured convergence: 443.82 (split), 425.31 (all-CPU), 405.22 (dense control) at npl=8 - three different placements, one ceiling. The only measured lever that moves it is top-k reduction, which cuts the FLOPs: +21% to +63% at k=4 (prereg #22).
laws.scope: GTX 1060. A modern GPU has 10-100x the FLOPs; this wall is a property of the card, not of llama.cpp.
laws.wired_into: the research agenda: asymmetric top-k Stage 2 (U-07) is the one open prefill lever

levers.claim: Partial MoE expert offload (-ot blk.(K..N).ffn_.*_exps.=CPU --no-mmap) beats both all-VRAM and all-CPU.
Sizing -ub from measured VRAM headroom (never pinning it) is worth up to 73% of prefill and avoids a 45% cliff.
levers.magnitude: 199.90 -> 345.89 where it applies; -45% where it does not

levers.claim: Evicting KV to host RAM (-nkvo 1) buys prefill on a VRAM-starved placement and costs decode.
levers.magnitude: 3.84x prefill on the split; -47% decode at 16k depth

levers.claim: N-gram speculation is worth ~4.7x on copy-regime output AT ~3-BIT QUANTIZATION - and the multiplier SHRINKS with bits (3.39x at Q3_K_M), because speculation converts a bandwidth-bound problem into a compute-bound one.
levers.magnitude: Flagship, split placement, chat template, coherent output (prereg #28): edit task 2.41x (20.73 -> 50.04 tok/s, 89% acceptance) - ABOVE the 41.1 raw-decode wall; novel code 0.98x at 0% acceptance; novel prose 1.00x. Dense 7B (original): 2.10x on code. The original 'code vs prose' framing was a proxy: code tasks are usually copy-heavy and prose tasks usually novel, but the edit IS the variable. Also measured: the staked temp-0 raw-continuation harness produced a repetition loop whose 100% acceptance inflated ngram to 1.82-1.96x on garbage output - caught by reading the completion, re-measured under the chat template. COMPOSITION (prereg #35): speculation and q8_0 KV are independent multipliers - stack measured 49.42 vs 47.61 predicted from the product (ratio 1.038, no destructive interference), and output is byte-identical at both KV precisions. DRAFT-LENGTH SWEEP (prereg #36, position-controlled): --spec-ngram-simple-size-m 24/48/96/192/384/768 -> 46.10 / 49.80 / 65.00 / 78.01 / 90.33 / 89.82 tok/s, ALL byte-identical output. Best is m=384 at 90.33 = +81% over the default and 2.2x this box's raw-decode wall. Mechanism: m is a per-round draft BUDGET, so raising it delivers the SAME accepted tokens in FEWER verify rounds (drafted/accepted freeze at 1100/735 from m=192 on while throughput still climbs) - each round costs a full weight read. m=768 returns byte-identical counts to m=384 because the n-gram store has no longer matching spans: the plateau is the DRAFTER's ceiling, not the hardware's. LOOKUP-LENGTH SWEEP (prereg #37, position-controlled, all at size-m 384): size-n 20/12/6/4/2 -> 77.61 / 90.67 / 105.52 / 108.41 / 81.98 tok/s, all byte-identical. Best is n=4 at 108.41 = 5.0x the 21.6 no-speculation baseline and 2.6x the 41.1 raw-decode wall. Stacking ngram-cache is a 10% REGRESSION (97.16).
levers.evidence: prereg #10 (Law 6 arm S-e, dense), prereg #28 (flagship, re-scoped); prereg #36 (draft-length sweep); prereg #37 (lookup length + stacking); prereg #40 (quality scoping, with same-model confound control)
levers.scope: llama-server only - llama-cli silently ignores --spec-type (measured as a 1.00x that was the flag not existing) QUANTIZATION SCOPE (prereg #40): the multiplier is NOT invariant in bits. Same model (Qwen3-Coder-30B): Q2_K_L 4.63x, Q3_K_M 3.39x = 0.73 of it. Two different models at ~10.5 GB both give 4.6-4.8x, so bits is the variable, not the model.
levers.counterintuitive_note: Acceptance rate is the WRONG optimisation target. It FALLS from 100% (m=24) to 66.8% (m=384) while throughput rises from 46 to 90 tok/s. Rejected drafts are nearly free; skipped weight reads are not. Anyone tuning speculation by maximising acceptance will tune it backwards.
levers.the_hidden_variable: Across n=20->4 drafted tokens move only +5% (1068->1121) while throughput moves +40%. Tokens drafted is not the variable; VERIFY ROUNDS are - the same drafted tokens delivered in fewer, longer runs, each round costing one full weight read. Confirmed independently in #36 (throughput rose while drafted/accepted froze). Neither draft_n nor acceptance measures it. n=2 is the proof: it drafts the MOST (1486) and accepts the most (775) and is 25% SLOWER than n=4, because a 2-token lookup matches noise and produces many short quickly-rejected runs.
levers.identity_scope_note: Temp-0 identity claims in this project compare MATCHED REQUEST INDEX. Measured in prereg #38: request 1 and request 2 of the same server produce different output (sha 65985276565a vs 28a5c1e1c014) with AND without speculation - that is prompt-cache reuse (cache_prompt defaults true; reused KV is not bit-identical to freshly computed KV), not a speculation effect. Across arms at the same request index, every speculation configuration is byte-identical. Earlier harnesses reported only the last request's sha, so they were comparing req2 to req2 - valid, but blind to this.

levers.claim: Depth-aware protection of fragile tensors buys quality at near-zero size.
The probe's band search beats APEX's symmetric prior: real fragility is strictly monotonic and LATE-weighted, not symmetric across depth.
levers.magnitude: S-1 HIT sharper than staked (reference PPL 5.4298, WikiText, 40-layer source); out-of-domain rematch confirms calibration generalises - 25.6% on KL against the Q8_0 parent, on a corpus the imatrix never saw

levers.claim: Dense models have a measurable PROTECTED share of activated bytes - the attention tensors that stay high-precision - so dense speed responds to bit-width instead of being flat in it.
levers.magnitude: DENSE_PROTECTED_SHARE = 0.214, the mean attention share read from GGUF tensor shapes: 10.8% Qwen2.5-7B, 20.2% gemma4-12B, 25.1% Qwen3.5-4B, 29.6% Qwen3-0.6B
levers.evidence: prereg #17 (dense-activation-model) - P-1 HIT, P-2 HIT decisively, P-3 MISS

levers.claim: Quantizing the KV cache to q8_0 pays AT DEPTH ONLY - it dominates the shipped 'evict KV' row at 16k, and it is a ~6% net COST at chat-length context, where the dequant work is paid every token for a negligible byte saving.
levers.magnitude: split placement, -fa 1, r=3, one session. tg32 @ d16384: q8_0-in-VRAM 10.59 vs -nkvo-1 3.48 (3.04x); tg32 @ d0: 20.18 vs 17.06 (+18%); pp2048: 382.17 vs 386.14 (-1.0%, inside the error bar). Against f16 KV in VRAM, q8_0 is +37.0% at depth and -3.3% at d0. DEPTH CONDITION (prereg #35): at ~1k context on the same split placement, q8_0 KV measures 20.38 vs f16 21.64 = 0.942x - a 5.8% loss. The +37% is a 16k-depth result and must not be quoted at short context.
levers.evidence: prereg #25 (kv-cache-quantization); prereg #35 (the depth condition and the composition test)
levers.scope: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q2_K, split placement, GTX 1060 6GB - one architecture, one flag varied
levers.wired_into: NOT SHIPPED. Blocked on the perplexity cost, a condition written into the stake before any number existed: D-01 killed a 1.335x lever for costing 1.206x perplexity, and 3.04x is exactly when skipping that step is most tempting.

levers.claim: quantprobe's numbers are SINGLE-STREAM and understate aggregate server throughput by roughly 2x.
levers.magnitude: ~2.0x at 8 slots, saturating by about 4 (see C-06 for the full table)
levers.scope: GTX 1060 6GB; the ratio is unmeasured on modern hardware
levers.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py concurrency disclosure in the plan output

levers.claim: Prefix caching (cache_prompt) collapses TTFT on repeated-document workloads - the asymptote moves, and it dwarfs every placement decision for RAG/document-QA.
levers.magnitude: 29.3x on the second question against a 2k-token document (5380.8 -> 183.4 ms prompt time; only the 8-token suffix is processed); 109.6x on an identical repeat; decode untouched (21.73-21.89 across all cells)
levers.scope: llama-server, one process - a restart is cold; serves many-questions-one-document, not fresh documents

levers.claim: I-quant (IQ*) files are catastrophic on CPU tiers - 2.7x slower than K-quants at the same size - and the planner now warns before a user pays that silently.
levers.magnitude: Pure-CPU decode, same dense 7B, r=3: IQ3_XS 10.6 GB/s effective vs Q2_K 28.4 / Q4_K_M 29.7. K-format dequant is bandwidth-shaped on AVX2; the IQ codebook lookup is compute-shaped and 4 cores cannot hide it. In VRAM the IQ formats measured mid-pack (the eta study), so the warning fires ONLY on host-resident placements.
levers.evidence: prereg #31 arm F; C-05 fourth instance
levers.scope: host-resident placements, AVX2-class CPUs; VRAM placements explicitly excluded from the warning

levers.claim: The quality-vs-speed frontier UNDER SPECULATION - the table a person needs to pick a model for their machine, which no published benchmark provides because everyone quotes raw decode.
levers.magnitude: 2016 desktop (GTX 1060 6GB + DDR4-3000), 30B-A3B MoE, single user, copy-regime output, split placement + ngram-simple m384 n4, request 1 of a fresh server: ~3-bit (Q2_K / Q2_K_L) = 99 tok/s at x1.05-1.07 planner quality cost; ~3.9-bit (Q3_K_M) = 59 tok/s at x1.02-1.05. Raw decode for the same rows is 21 and 17. So the published raw numbers understate achievable speed by 3.4-4.8x on work whose output reuses its context.
levers.evidence: prereg #40 (with same-model confound control); #36/#37 for the tuning
levers.scope: copy-regime output only - novel generation gains nothing (D-10). One box, one model family.
levers.wired_into: quantprobe/plan.py:speculation_advice carries the multiplier and its quantization scope

dead_ends.claim: Reducing expert count (top-k 8->4) for DECODE is strictly dominated by simply quantizing further.
dead_ends.magnitude: k=4: 1.335x speed for 1.206x perplexity. Bit ladder: 1.424x for 1.048x - faster AND 4x cheaper.

dead_ends.claim: Intra-tensor VQ on Gemma MLP weights cannot pay - the stream is white.
k-means matched-rate VQ is a runtime trap - decode cost swamps the compression win.
Two frontier cells are dominated on BOTH axes and must never be recommended.
dead_ends.magnitude: all-experts-CPU + KV evicted 336.31/15.82; split + KV VRAM + ub2048 163.39/20.13

dead_ends.claim: REOPENED 2026-07-27 (prereg #32), scoped. Was: 'forking llama.cpp is not worth it (1-6%)'. The fork is still refuted - but the CPU MUL_MAT_ID expert path is measured to leave ~40% of DRAM bandwidth uncaptured, the memory-system excuse is refuted by microbenchmark, and an UPSTREAM PR against that one path has a real, bounded prize.
dead_ends.magnitude: Shuffled 2MB expert-slab reads: 24.56 GB/s vs 23.88 sequential (+2.9%, noise) - the memory system is indifferent to the scatter. MoE CPU path: 16.0 GB/s at 4 threads where dense reaches 28.4 identically threaded; thread scaling 1x/1.64x/2.17x. Prize: host share at dense efficiency = +65%, raw decode 22.25 -> ~30 realistic, 41 perfect. Still below free speculation (50-59), so the prize matters for NOVEL generation specifically, where speculation is closed (D-10). PROFILED (prereg #33): the marginal expert GEMV runs AT the wall (23.1 GB/s, k-sweep slope 4.19 ms/expert), expert-major dispatch is a measured null, and the deficit is ~32 ms/token of FIXED per-op machinery - leading suspect the CPU graph executor's per-op thread barrier on a small-op-heavy MoE graph. The upstream target is the executor, not MUL_MAT_ID.
dead_ends.evidence: prereg #32 (fork gate); prereg #27 (the decomposition); prereg #31 (dense kernel at the wall); prereg #20 (the original phase-split ceiling analysis this verdict was first built on); prereg #33 (the profile)
dead_ends.scope: EXPLICITLY NOT the disk-streaming tier - ds4 shows ~7x there
dead_ends.wired_into: FUTURE.md upstream-PR target; the fork and the from-scratch runtime remain refuted on measured grounds

dead_ends.claim: The sub-4-bit decode collapse is a FORMAT property, not a bit-width property - gating on bits was wrong.
Frequency-ranked MoE expert residency is NOT reachable from stock llama.cpp, and at our VRAM ratio it would buy single digits anyway.
dead_ends.magnitude: ktransformers' own matched-VRAM table (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-FP8, 4x RTX 4090, ShareGPT): frequency vs front-loading is +2.5% to +5.3% in the 10-30% GPU-residency band we actually live in - against U-02's staked +15% to +40%. The staked band is reached only by DYNAMIC runtime re-placement (+18% to +27%), which needs a fork, at which point D-05 applies.
dead_ends.evidence: E-01 study of kvcache-ai/ktransformers (doc/en/kt-kernel/experts-sched-Tutorial.md; SOSP'25 paper); E-02 study of PowerInfer
dead_ends.scope: MoE expert placement via stock llama.cpp -ot, low VRAM-residency ratio
dead_ends.why_the_protocol_was_impossible: U-02's protocol said 'build an -ot regex from the top-N experts'. It cannot work: llama.cpp fuses ALL experts of a layer into one 3D tensor (blk.N.ffn_gate_exps.weight, {n_embd, n_ff, n_expert}) consumed by MUL_MAT_ID, and -ot matches tensor NAMES - so its finest MoE unit is 'all experts of layer N', which IS the contiguous split V-01 already ships. The ktransformers authors say so directly: they had to patch llama.cpp to get expert-level offloading for their own comparison.
dead_ends.and_it_corroborates_v01: Their 'front-loading' strategy is the exact semantic twin of our contiguous split, and it BEATS 'uniform' at most ratios (73.65 vs 65.25 at 50%, +12.9%). Our index-based choice was made because it is what -ot can express; it turns out to be the better of the two statistics-free strategies.
dead_ends.and_powerinfer_does_not_support_the_prem: PowerInfer's skew is DENSE ReLU FFN neurons (17-26% of neurons carry 80% of activations), never MoE expert selection - 'Mixture-of-Experts' appears once in the paper, in a citation. It also never ran the matched-memory frequency-vs-index comparison U-02 assumed it had, and it assigns individual NEURONS to GPU or CPU, which -ot cannot express either.

dead_ends.claim: Pinned host memory is ALREADY in use for every host-resident row quantprobe recommends - there is no PCIe headroom to reclaim.
dead_ends.magnitude: U-03's predicted '+30% on host-resident prefill if currently pageable' resolves to 0%.
dead_ends.evidence: U-03 source study: -ot=CPU re-runs buffer selection over the CPU buft list (ACCEL -> GPU-host -> CPU-extra -> CPU); on a CUDA build the GPU-host entry is CUDA_Host, allocated by cudaMallocHost. llama-model-loader.cpp:1197-1205 demotes it back to pageable IF use_mmap is true.
dead_ends.wired_into: U-03 withdrawn; the --no-mmap smoke invariant is now known to be load-bearing for a second reason
dead_ends.the_conditional_that_matters: The pinning is CONDITIONAL on --no-mmap, which quantprobe always emits on -ot=CPU rows. llama-bench defaults use_mmap=true, so a run without it is pageable - and that is the identified mechanism behind the ~21 percentage points prereg #13 attributed to --no-mmap alone. We had the right flag for an incompletely understood reason.

dead_ends.claim: The CHAINING drafter (ngram-mod) loses to the dumb contiguous-copy drafter (ngram-simple) on copy-regime output, and its cross-request table POISONS rather than helps.
dead_ends.magnitude: Request 1 of a fresh server, edit task, split placement: ngram-simple m384/n4 109.52 tok/s vs ngram-mod tuned 86.42-86.63 (-21%) and ngram-mod at defaults 57.41 (-48%). Raising n_max 512->1024 changes nothing (556 drafted in both): the chain dies on a hash miss long before either cap. Request 2 is 17-25% SLOWER than request 1 (86.42->71.75, 86.63->64.65) while drafting 75% MORE (556->976) at collapsed acceptance (65.6%->39.3%).
dead_ends.evidence: prereg #38; source study of llama.cpp@f113e02 (speculative.cpp:1860-1872 chaining, 1811-1813 no-clear accumulation, ngram-map.cpp:96 the single-span copy)
dead_ends.scope: copy-regime output (edits/refactors/quoting) on Qwen3-30B-A3B, reference box. A workload whose output is NOT near-copy of context was not tested and mod may differ there.
dead_ends.wired_into: no code change - the shipped ngram-simple flags already carry the winner
dead_ends.why_the_smarter_drafter_loses: Mod's 4.2M-slot table stores ONE successor per hash slot, no key, overwrite-on-write - so every chaining step can silently be a collision, and the chain is autoregressive, so one wrong step corrupts everything after it. Simple's contiguous copy is verified-correct BY CONSTRUCTION: it reproduces text that actually occurred. On output that is a near-copy of the context, freedom is not the constraint and the smarter drafter's error compounds.
dead_ends.and_it_explains_D_10: This is the source-level explanation of the #30 replay artifact, now measured in the OPPOSITE direction: there, mod's accumulated table made a repeated identical request look fast; here, on a real edit task, the same accumulation makes it slower. Either way the number is not reproducible on fresh input - which is why request 1 of a fresh server is the only figure this project quotes for mod.

contradictions.claim: The GLM kvp values are wrong in BOTH directions and by 2x - not the 30-60x we believed. glm-744b is 2.10x too LARGE, glm-air is 2x too SMALL, and the two are related by a transposition.
contradictions.magnitude: GLM-5.2 is MLA + DeepSeek Sparse Attention (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM): 78 layers, kv_lora_rank 512, qk_rope_head_dim 64. By quantprobe's own MLA convention that is 78 x (512+64) x 2 = 89,856 B/token against a shipped 188,416 - 2.10x too large. Separately GLM-4.5-Air is plain GQA: 46 x 8 x (128+128) x 2 = 188,416, EXACTLY the value sitting in the glm-744b row, against a shipped glm-air value of 94,208 - 2x too small.
contradictions.evidence: C-01 research from primary configs (zai-org/GLM-5.2 config.json; Glm4MoeForCausalLM configs). NOT back-solved from any observed datapoint.
contradictions.next_action: Verify the config fields directly before changing a shipped number, then fix BOTH rows in quantprobe/plan.py and mirror into docs/index.html and docs/simulator.html. llama.cpp does not implement the DSA indexer yet, so 89,856 is the right target for what we predict against; the indexer would add ~5,376 B/token on top.
contradictions.lesson: Our stated belief - '30-60x too large' - was itself wrong by more than an order of magnitude, and it came from reasoning about a symptom instead of reading the architecture. The register had recorded that belief with the same confidence as a measurement.

contradictions.claim: The all-in-VRAM efficiency eta is not a constant, not a per-format constant, and not a bytes-weighted mix of per-type constants. It varies 0.319-0.561 (76%) across seven measured models on ONE GPU, and no parameter the tool currently has access to predicts it.
contradictions.magnitude: Implied eta from the 7 ratchet points, same box, plan --gguf: gemma4-12b custom mix 0.319 (the only OVER-prediction, +9.8%) | Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 0.357 | Qwen2.5-7B Q2_K 0.377 | Qwen2.5-7B IQ3_XS 0.384 | Bonsai-27B Q1_0 0.445 | Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M 0.464 | Qwen2.5-7B Q4_K_M 0.561. The law assumes 0.35 for all of them.
contradictions.evidence: prereg #24 (eta-vram-bytes-per-token) + prereg #15 (law4-v3-overhead-term) + weights/data/prereg24_eta_bytes_per_token.log; verify.py layer 3 FAILS on this
contradictions.wired_into: disclosed in CLI output as 'a floor, not a ceiling' - but the disclosed band (2%-67%) is itself now too narrow
contradictions.why_it_is_the_top_item: It is the placement most users land on, it is the one we undersell, and underselling -ngl 99 pushes people toward complicated offload placements that are actually SLOWER for them. Every other finding in this register is about configurations that are harder than the default.
contradictions.what_the_data_rules_out: (a) FIXED OVERHEAD - refuted by prereg #15. (b) GPU CLOCK STATE - refuted by its own prediction (cold 144.21 vs warm 143.37). (c) GATE MODEL-SELECTION - the 7B misses by more than the 0.5B. (d) BYTES PER TOKEN - refuted by prereg #24's control, which has fewer bytes and higher eta. (e) MONOTONE IN BIT-WIDTH - refuted here: Q8_0 at 8.5 bits gives 0.357, LOWER than Q2_K at 2.8 bits (0.377). (f) A PER-FORMAT CONSTANT - refuted here: two models both labelled Q4_K_M give 0.464 and 0.561, a 21% spread that no single per-format value can absorb. (g) A BYTES-WEIGHTED MIX OVER ACTUAL TENSOR TYPES - the most promising candidate, and it does not close. The mix genuinely differs and in the right direction (the 4B 'Q4_K_M' is only 54.9% Q4_K with 37.8% Q6_K, while the 7B is 73.3% Q4_K), but solving the linear system across all points forces a NEGATIVE eta for Q5_K or for Q2_K depending on which points are used. It is not a linear mixture.
contradictions.leading_hypothesis: WITHIN one architecture the pattern is clean and monotone in the dominant tensor type - Qwen2.5-7B goes Q2_K 0.377 -> IQ3_XS 0.384 -> Q4_K_M 0.561. ACROSS architectures it does not transfer at all, and the two worst outliers are both architecturally unusual: gemma4-12b (sliding-window attention, and the only model we OVER-predict) and Bonsai-27B (linear-attention hybrid, already flagged under Law 2). So eta looks like a property of (architecture x tensor mix x kernel), which is not a constant and is not something the tool can derive from the inputs it has.
contradictions.next_action: STOP FITTING. Six candidate corrections have now been refuted, four of them mine. The remaining honest moves are about DISCLOSURE, not calibration, and one of them is a published-number decision that is the maintainer's to make rather than mine: verify.py layer 3 applies a single +/-25% band to regimes whose measured accuracy differs enormously, and for all-in-VRAM that band is simply false - 13 measurements put the regime at +12% to +85%, always in the same direction. Either the band becomes regime-aware and one-sided (honest, but it changes the tool's headline accuracy claim and must be published as a correction), or layer 3 stops selecting an all-in-VRAM model to test a law that regime is known to break. Widening a band to make a test pass would be goalpost-moving; stating a measured per-regime accuracy is not - but the distinction depends on it being published loudly, which is a call to make deliberately.
contradictions.also_establishes: Between-session drift is 10-13% on decode against sub-1% within-session error bars, now measured three times on the same 4B model: 27.30 (07-26), 30.89 (07-27 early), 30.03 (07-27 late). C-04 recorded this for prefill; it holds for decode too, and it bounds what any single session can conclude.
contradictions.direction_of_the_error: A floor with an exception is not a floor, and two earlier versions of this entry were incoherent in exactly that way ('faster every time' beside a listed over-prediction; then 'floor with one measured exception'). The coherent form is a ONE-SIDED BOUND placed BELOW the worst measurement: real >= 0.90x predicted, 13 of 13 benchmarks (worst point gemma4-12b at 0.910x), falsified by any single measurement below it. Same logical form as the law's +/-25% claim - a bound stated with its evidence that a future measurement can kill - just asymmetric, because the measured error is asymmetric.
contradictions.what_shipped: verify.py:e2e_band - layer 3's accuracy band is now PER REGIME. All-in-VRAM is -15/+90, the other regimes keep +/-25% because that is where the layer-4 anchors validate it. The lower bound is the load-bearing half: it is what fails if the tool ever becomes OPTIMISTIC, which is the direction that costs a user something. Published as a correction in README and CHANGELOG rather than edited quietly - a measured per-regime accuracy is honest, but only if it is stated at least as loudly as the number it replaces.

contradictions.claim: verify.py layer 3 is sensitive to GPU clock state - the same 0.5B model measures across the +/-25% band depending on whether the card is warm.
contradictions.scope: verify layer 3 on the smallest model
contradictions.next_action: either fix the clock state before measuring, or stop selecting the smallest model - a 0.5B decode is overhead-dominated and is the worst possible test of a bandwidth law

contradictions.claim: Absolute prefill figures are not stable across invocation shapes, only ratios are.
contradictions.magnitude: split/nkvo0/ub2048 measured 85.47 swept alone vs 161.59 in the full matrix
contradictions.next_action: any future use of an absolute figure needs its own controlled run

contradictions.claim: A QUANTIZED BYTE IS NOT A BYTE. Below a format-specific threshold, bytes removed from the bandwidth bill reappear as dequantisation compute - so every efficiency constant fitted at ONE format is wrong at another. Measured three times.
contradictions.magnitude: D-06: the sub-4-bit decode collapse is a weight-FORMAT property, not bit-width. C-02: eta is a weight-FORMAT-CLASS property - sub-4-bit 0.425-0.443 vs 4-bit 0.510-0.631, against one assumed 0.35. #25: ETA_KV holds to 8 bits and collapses below - q8_0 KV delivers 0.563 of f16's KV time against a 0.53 nominal ratio (+6.2%, the model works), while q4_0 delivers 0.532 against 0.28 nominal (+90%, the model fails) and buys only +2.0% over q8_0. FOURTH INSTANCE (prereg #31): on the CPU tier, IQ formats deliver 10.6 GB/s vs ~29 for K-quants at identical size - dequant cost is format-shaped, again. FIFTH INSTANCE (prereg #40): on the speculation axis. Bytes rise 1.299x from Q2_K_L to Q3_K_M; raw decode cost rises 1.222x (tracks bytes, as Law 4 requires) but SPECULATED decode cost rises 1.670x - 1.37x faster than bytes. A verify round processes ~50 tokens at once, which #26 measured to be compute-bound, and once compute-bound the extra bits cost extra DEQUANTISATION on every one of those tokens rather than extra bytes moved.
contradictions.wired_into: nothing yet - this is a lint waiting to be written
contradictions.next_action: Three instances is a pattern, not a coincidence. Audit EVERY remaining efficiency constant for the same assumption and add a gate check that refuses a constant fitted at a single format. The saturation point differs by quantity - ~4-bit for weights, ~8-bit for KV - so the lint cannot be a fixed threshold; it must demand that the constant was MEASURED across formats.

contradictions.claim: Batched decode saturates at roughly 2x by about 4 concurrent slots, identically across architecture, placement and memory tier - and nothing this project models explains it.
contradictions.magnitude: Aggregate decode, npl 1 -> 8, one session: split 21.93 -> 44.48 (2.03x); all-experts-CPU 19.89 -> 37.70 (1.90x); DENSE 7B fully in VRAM 22.47 -> 50.48 (2.25x). Per-step time grows 3.56x while weight bytes per step are unchanged, so weight amortisation works as expected - the cost that grows is per-sequence work, unidentified.
contradictions.scope: GTX 1060 6GB, llama-batched-bench, npp 512 / ntg 128. A 2016 card without tensor cores is exactly where a batched-decode ceiling would appear first.
contradictions.wired_into: disclosed in the CLI; NOT modelled
contradictions.hypotheses_already_refuted: (a) Host-residency amortisation - staked as P-2 and refuted BY DIRECTION: the placement with MORE host-resident weight gained LESS (1.90x vs 2.03x). (b) MoE routing divergence across slots - refuted by the dense control, which saturates at 2.25x, barely above the MoE split. No mechanism is named here on purpose: in this project the first mechanism guess has been wrong four times, and each wrong guess survived exactly as long as nobody built a control that could kill it.
contradictions.next_action: Run the identical sweep on ANY modern GPU. It costs one command and decides whether this is a law or a museum piece. Until then quantprobe must not model concurrency - it can only disclose it.
contradictions.the_part_that_did_work: PREFILL shows the staked mechanism plainly: arm A gains 2.12x from batching against arm S's 1.44x, because A has the most host-resident weight to amortise - exactly L-09. But all three arms converge to ~405-445 t/s, a ceiling that caps the effect before it can change any recommendation.

contradictions.claim: CPU decode speed depends ~40% on the OpenMP runtime the binary was BUILT with - a variable no hardware spec exposes and the tool cannot currently see.
contradictions.magnitude: Same source, same box, same model, tg32 t=4: gcc+libgomp (mingw, kernel-semaphore barriers, no spin phase) 11.92; gcc+GGML_OPENMP=OFF (ggml spin barrier) 16.64 (+40%); MSVC+libomp default 13.28; +KMP_BLOCKTIME=infinite 13.89. ~2070 barriers/token; the mechanism, not the count, was most of the tax.
contradictions.evidence: prereg #34; the E3 per-op profiler (barrier 30.8 -> 10.8 ms/token); barrier-map desk research (symbol-level libgomp evidence)
contradictions.scope: pure-CPU decode, 4-core Windows box. The split placement runs on libomp (mostly spinning already); CUDA+no-OpenMP is unmeasured.
contradictions.wired_into: UPSTREAM ISSUE FILED: ggml-org/llama.cpp#26200 (2026-07-27, FedericoTs). Carries the three-build A/B, the E3 barrier ledger, the symbol-level libgomp evidence, a copy-paste repro, and both supporting nulls.
contradictions.next_action: Watch ggml-org/llama.cpp#26200 for maintainer response. Remaining open: whether the finding transfers to a CUDA build - MEASURED NOT to transfer to the shipped split config via the libomp spin-policy A/B (20.12 vs 20.56, bars overlap), but a CUDA + GGML_OPENMP=OFF build is untested here (no nvcc on this box).

contradictions.claim: quantprobe SUMS multi-device bandwidth, which models tensor-parallel (--split-mode row). llama.cpp's DEFAULT is --split-mode LAYER, which is SERIAL - so for any multi-GPU user on defaults the tool over-predicts decode by roughly the device count.
contradictions.magnitude: agg_bw() returns sum(v)*eff for a device list (quantprobe/plan.py). Under a layer split each GPU holds a disjoint subset of layers and they run SEQUENTIALLY within a token, so t = sum(bytes_i/BW_i): two IDENTICAL cards give the same decode speed as one card that could hold everything - capacity, not bandwidth. The tool would predict ~2x. For HETEROGENEOUS cards it is worse than wrong in magnitude, it is wrong in DIRECTION: adding a slow card to a fast one makes a fitting model SLOWER (3090 alone 1.30 ms/token vs 3090+1060 at 20/80 = 2.31 ms), while the tool predicts a gain.
contradictions.evidence: first-principles from llama.cpp split-mode semantics + Law 4; NOT yet measured - this box has one GPU
contradictions.scope: multi-device inputs (--vram 24,6 style). Single-GPU predictions unaffected. Row-split may approach the summed model, minus sync.
contradictions.wired_into: NOT FIXED - no second GPU to measure on
contradictions.next_action: Highest-value thing a two-GPU contributor can measure. Until then the honest interim is a WARNING on multi-device input stating that the estimate assumes row-split and that layer-split (the default) adds capacity rather than bandwidth. The moment a second GPU exists on this box, this is the first measurement - it is also the same session that unblocks C-02.

untried.claim: Speculation and batching may compose (5x x 2x) or contend for the same forward pass - staked in prereg #39 and WITHDRAWN incomplete when the project's priority moved to single-user quality.
untried.hypothesis: Batching amortises one weight read across N slots (#26: ~2.0-2.25x, saturating by 4); speculation amortises it across k tokens within a slot (#36/#37: 4.7x at ~3-bit). They attack the same denominator by different means. The interference mechanism is real though: with continuous batching, one slot's 384-token verify batch may monopolise the forward pass other slots need, and the MoE expert-union tax (Law 6) grows with batch diversity.
untried.predicted_effect: staked in #39: aggregate >= 150 tok/s at -np 4 with speculation, and batching's multiplier surviving to within 80% with speculation on
untried.cost: 1 hour - two arms remain (-np 4 with and without speculation); the harness exists at weights/data/prereg39_spec_x_batch.log
untried.why_it_is_promising: it is the only remaining measured-multiplier composition, and it decides whether one cheap box serves one person fast or several people adequately
untried.protocol: resume prereg #39 arms C and D; report aggregate AND per-request (they diverge 2.3x - see the withdrawal note)
